Quantum field (Φ(x))

Words: 58
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum field is an operator-valued distribution on spacetime: smearing Φ(x) against a smooth test function gives an operator, whereas pointwise products can require renormalization. For example, a free complex scalar field contains particle annihilation operators and antiparticle creation operators. Its microcausality condition makes field commutators vanish at spacelike separation. For fermions, the corresponding locality condition uses anticommutators. This combines quantum operators with the spacetime locality of a quantum field theory.

Algebraic quantum field theory

Words: 281 Articles: 3
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Algebraic quantum field theory assigns an observable algebra A(O) to each suitable spacetime region O. Inclusion of regions implies inclusion of algebras, and spacelike-separated algebras commute under microcausality. A state is a positive normalized functional on the observable algebra, so its restriction to a region specifies expectation values and correlations for that algebra. Spectrum conditions restrict translation representations, while primitive causality and time-slice axioms constrain the dynamics; these are different assumptions.

Time-slice axiom

Words: 76
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The time-slice axiom says that an algebra generated in an arbitrarily thin suitable neighbourhood of a Cauchy surface generates the algebra of its causal development. For O such a neighbourhood in its development D(O), this is A(O)=A(D(O)). Precise global and local versions can differ in the regions to which they apply. For a local hyperbolic field equation, later fields can be represented using the initial field and its conjugate momentum in the corresponding domain of dependence.

Primitive causality

Words: 74
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Primitive causality is a dynamical completeness condition: the state restricted to a suitable initial spacetime region determines its expectations throughout that region's domain of dependence. Algebraically one requires the later domain-of-dependence observable algebra to be contained in the initial algebra, under the identifications supplied by the dynamics. A local time-slice axiom gives this property for a neighbourhood of a Cauchy slice. Knowledge of the full restricted state, including correlations, is required; knowing only mean initial fields is insufficient.

Spectrum condition (Sp(P)⊆V+​)

Words: 68
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
In a translation-covariant quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, the joint spectrum of the energy-momentum generators is required to lie in the closed future light cone. With signature (+,−,−,−) this means p0≥0 and p2≥0. The spectrum condition implements a positive-energy stability requirement in every inertial frame. It constrains the Fourier support and analyticity of vacuum correlation functions but does not by itself assert spacelike commutation or an initial-value property.

Positive-energy spectrum condition (specPμ⊆V+​)

Words: 44
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The joint energy-momentum spectrum lies in the closed forward light cone. In axiomatic quantum field theory, this condition permits analytic continuation of Wightman functions in suitable complex spacetime domains. Together with Lorentz invariance, microcausality and the positivity of the physical state space, it is one of the hypotheses behind the CPT theorem.

Canonical transformation of mode operators (ai′​=∑j​(Uij​aj​+Vij​aj†​))

Words: 729 Articles: 15
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A linear change of creation operators and annihilation operators is canonical when it preserves their defining brackets. For finitely many bosonic modes, the canonical commutation relations require UU†−VV†=I and UVT−VUT=0. For fermions, the canonical anticommutation relations instead require UU†+VV†=I and UVT+VUT=0. A Bogoliubov transformation uses such mixing to diagonalize a quadratic Hamiltonian or relate different vacuum descriptions. Infinite-mode unitary implementation has further conditions, as in bosonic mode mixing implementability.

Bogoliubov transformation

Words: 675 Articles: 14
Canonical transformation of mode operators OurBigBook.com
A Bogoliubov transformation is a canonical transformation of mode operators mixing creation operators and annihilation operators. It diagonalizes quadratic Hamiltonians or relates different vacuum descriptions. Bosonic and fermionic canonical bracket constraints differ. A nonzero creation-mixing coefficient makes its vacuum contain particles relative to the original mode decomposition.

Nambu spinor (Ψk​=(ck​,c−k†​)T)

Words: 213 Articles: 3
Bogoliubov transformation OurBigBook.com
A Nambu spinor groups an annihilation operator with an opposite-momentum creation operator to express pairing in a quadratic Hamiltonian as a matrix problem. Its components are not independent: the spinor at −k is related to conjugated components at k. This redundancy must be accounted for when summing energies and normal ordering constants. Component phases are a convention and change the displayed off-diagonal matrix entries.
Self-paired spinless fermion mode (k≡−k(mod2π))
Words: 55
Nambu spinor OurBigBook.com
In a unit-spacing periodic spinless chain, self-paired momenta are k=0 and, when available, k=π. An anomalous pair of the same creation operator vanishes by the canonical anticommutation relations. Such a mode is a single normal number level, filled or empty according to its energy sign, rather than a two-distinct-mode Bogoliubov transformation. This excludes the paired-angle construction at those special momenta.
Bosonic Nambu normal-ordering shift (ak​ak†​=1+ak†​ak​)
Words: 59
Nambu spinor OurBigBook.com
In a bosonic Nambu spinor expression, the second diagonal entry commonly contains a−k​a−k†​. The canonical commutation relations add one constant per mode when this is normal ordered. For an antiferromagnetic chain coefficient JS, rewriting the quadratic Hamiltonian as a full Nambu sum therefore changes the exterior constant from −NJS2 to −NJS(S+1). Omitting the shift corrupts the ground-state energy even when the dispersion is unchanged.
Ising-chain Nambu spinor (Ψk​=(ck​,−ic−k†​)T)
Words: 43
Nambu spinor OurBigBook.com
With Fourier convention cn​=N−1/2∑k​e−iknck​, the Transverse-field Ising model has H=J∑k​Ψk†​[(g−cosk)σz​−sinkσx​]Ψk​. Expanding the spinor retains the constant −JgN and pairs k with −k. The physical quasiparticle energy is twice the positive matrix eigenvalue times J, because both momentum partners occur in the Nambu sum.

Bosonic mode mixing implementability (∑i,j​∣βij​∣2<∞)

Words: 52
Bogoliubov transformation OurBigBook.com
A bounded invertible bosonic Bogoliubov transformation is unitarily implementable in the usual bosonic Fock space precisely when its creation-mixing part is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator. Without this condition, the transformation still preserves the algebraic canonical commutation relations, but its two vacua need not be vectors in a common Fock space. Equal nonzero squeezing in countably many independent modes is a simple counterexample.

Bosonic Bogoliubov diagonalization (ωk​=Ak2​−Bk2​​)

Words: 87 Articles: 1
Bogoliubov transformation OurBigBook.com
For real even coefficients with Ak​>∣Bk​∣, the quadratic Hamiltonian
H=∑k​[Ak​ak†​ak​+2Bk​​(ak​a−k​+ak†​a−k†​)]
(1)
is diagonalized by the Bogoliubov transformation ak​=coshθk​αk​−sinhθk​α−k†​, with tanh2θk​=Bk​/Ak​. The canonical commutation relations follow from cosh2θk​−sinh2θk​=1. The diagonal form is ∑k​[ωk​αk†​αk​+(ωk​−Ak​)/2], with ωk​=Ak2​−Bk2​​. The original-mode vacuum depletion is sinh2θk​=(Ak​/ωk​−1)/2. At Ak​=∣Bk​∣, the exact zero mode requires separate infrared treatment.
Bosonic Bogoliubov zero-point shift (ΔE0​=21​∑k​(Ek​−Ak​))
Words: 34
Bosonic Bogoliubov diagonalization OurBigBook.com
Canonical diagonalization of Ak​bk†​bk​ plus an anomalous pair term gives the vacuum shift (Ek​−Ak​)/2 per momentum. Thus H=C+21​∑k​(Ek​−Ak​)+∑k​Ek​αk†​αk​. The subtraction of Ak​/2 accompanies the quasiparticle zero-point term; omitting it changes the ground-state energy.

Canonical identities for a bosonic Bogoliubov transformation (AA†−BB†=I,ABT=BAT)

Words: 66
Bogoliubov transformation OurBigBook.com
For mode mixing ψi′​=∑j​(Aij​ψj​+Bij​ψ​j​), the Klein-Gordon inner product extracts ai′​=∑j​(Aij​aj​−Bij​aj†​). The canonical commutation relation is preserved exactly when AA†−BB†=I and ABT=BAT. These follow by computing [ai′​,ak′​†] and [ai′​,ak′​]; they are also the positive- and negative-frequency mode orthonormality identities. In infinitely many modes, convergence and the existence of a common bosonic Fock space representation require additional analysis; the expected total particle number is finite only if B is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator.

In-vacuum and out-vacuum

Words: 182 Articles: 4
Bogoliubov transformation OurBigBook.com
If a background is stationary in the remote past and future, positive-frequency modes in those two regions define an in-vacuum and an out-vacuum. The intervening time dependence generally makes the two mode bases differ by a Bogoliubov transformation.
Out-vacuum (bi​∣0out​⟩=0)
Words: 27
In-vacuum and out-vacuum OurBigBook.com
The state annihilated by every annihilation operator of the positive-frequency mode basis chosen in the asymptotic future. It need not coincide with the in-vacuum on a time-dependent spacetime.
In-vacuum (ai​∣0in​⟩=0)
Words: 29
In-vacuum and out-vacuum OurBigBook.com
The state annihilated by every annihilation operator of the positive-frequency mode basis chosen in the asymptotic past. A Bogoliubov transformation can make it contain particles when tested by future out-mode number operators.

uiout​=∑j​(αij​ujin​+βij​ujin∗​),

Out-mode number fluctuations in the in-vacuum (⟨Ns2​⟩=2ns2​+ns​+∣cs​∣2)
Words: 67
Particle number from Bogoliubov coefficients OurBigBook.com
If bs​=∑j​(Asj​aj​+Bsj​aj†​) and the state is the in-vacuum, put ns​=∑j​∣Bsj​∣2 and cs​=∑j​Asj​Bsj​. The canonical commutation relations give Ns2​=bs†2​bs2​+Ns​. Acting with bs2​ on the vacuum produces cs​∣0⟩ and a two-particle vector whose squared norm is 2ns2​, because its two possible vacuum contractions have equal contributions. This proves the displayed second moment and Var(Ns​)=ns​(ns​+1)+∣cs​∣2. A thermal-mode formula requires cs​=0; a general squeezed vacuum state need not satisfy that restriction.

Sudden frequency quench

α=2ω+​ω−​​ω+​+ω−​​,β=2ω+​ω−​​ω+​−ω−​​.
(4)
The initial vacuum therefore contains ∣β∣2 final particles in that mode.

Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum field theory with enough mutually compatible conserved quantities to constrain its dynamics exactly. In massive relativistic theories in one spatial dimension, suitable higher-spin conserved charges imply elastic factorized scattering: the set of incoming rapidities is preserved and multiparticle amplitudes are assembled from two-particle S-matrices.

Multiparticle quantum scattering is factorized when it decomposes into two-body scatterings without particle production or a new irreducible many-body amplitude. The independence of the answer from the order of exchanges imposes the Yang-Baxter equation. Classical pairwise additivity of soliton shifts is a corresponding property of integrable soliton collisions.

Scalar amplitudes give the displayed product. With internal indices, bound-state coupling tensors perform the projection. The Yang-Baxter equation makes different scattering orders consistent; factorization eliminates independent many-body scattering contributions.

For the unit-modulus hyperbolic scattering block with elementary mass m, a pair bound at rapidity difference iu has mass m2​=2mcos(u/2). Bootstrap fusion with another elementary particle gives a further direct pole at 3iu/2. It is inside the physical rapidity strip with positive imaginary residue only for 0<u<2π/3. In that range the new bound state has rest-frame constituent rapidities iu,0,−iu, so its energy is m(1+2cosu)=msin(3u/2)/sin(u/2). Charges add at the bound-state vertex. At u=2π/3 the apparent pole cancels; beyond that point it lies outside the physical strip. The formula is conditional on this particular scattering block and its direct-pole interpretation, not a universal three-body binding law.

A consistent associative algebra must give the same coefficients when a triple product is brought to decreasing or increasing rapidity order by either sequence of adjacent exchanges. Starting with three ordered rapidities, the adjacent-exchange sequences 121 and 212 must give identical coefficients for every final species word in the Faddeev-Zamolodchikov algebra. Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com

Composite operator OurBigBook.com
A contact term is a distribution supported where insertion points coincide. Its Fourier transform is local in momentum, typically polynomial. Renormalizing an operator product can require additive contact counterterms even if each operator has zero anomalous dimension.

Composite operator OurBigBook.com
Renormalization can relate bare operators to a matrix of renormalized operators, Oi,B​=Zij​Oj,R​. The corresponding anomalous dimension matrix acts on each insertion slot in the Callan-Symanzik equation.

Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The soft graviton theorem factorizes an amplitude with one low-energy graviton into the hard amplitude times a universal sum over external momenta. Gauge invariance of the soft factor requires energy-momentum conservation and universal gravitational coupling.

Soft graviton theorem OurBigBook.com
The Weinberg soft theorem constrains interactions of a massless particle by requiring its soft-emission amplitude to be invariant under shifts of an unphysical polarization. For helicity one it gives charge conservation, for helicity two it gives universal gravitational coupling, and for higher helicity it obstructs generic long-range interactions.

Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
An effective field theory describes phenomena below a chosen energy scale by retaining the relevant light fields and organizing local interactions by increasing suppression at that scale.

Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
An effective operator is a local interaction built from the retained fields in an effective field theory. Its coefficient records effects of heavier degrees of freedom, and allowed operators respect the relevant symmetries. In four dimensions an operator of mass dimension Δi​ has the displayed coefficient for dimensionless Ci​ and a heavy mass scale M. For example a dimension-six proton-decay operator has a coefficient proportional to M−2.

Words: 57
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A low-energy effective action retains the light degrees of freedom and describes the effects of heavier ones through local interactions and a derivative expansion. It can be obtained by matching an effective field theory or by a low-energy compactification. A Wilsonian effective action implements integration of high-energy modes with a scale cutoff. The quantum effective action that generates one-particle-irreducible vertices is a different construction; the two need not coincide.

Words: 41
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
An operator basis in effective field theory is an independent set of allowed local field operators at a chosen order, modulo relevant algebraic identities, integration by parts and permitted field redefinitions. Redundant operators can be removed without changing on-shell amplitudes, provided their coefficient shifts are accounted for. The basis depends on the light fields and symmetries.

Matching in effective field theory

Words: 48
Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
Matching in effective field theory fixes Wilson coefficients by requiring a low-energy theory and its ultraviolet completion to give the same low-energy amplitudes through a specified order. Both calculations must treat shared infrared physics consistently. Contributions from retained light particles are reproduced inside the effective field theory; their common nonanalytic parts are not replaced by arbitrary local heavy coefficients.

Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
A Wilson coefficient weights a local operator in an effective field theory. For an operator of mass dimension d in four spacetime dimensions, a dimensionless coefficient is conventionally accompanied by Λ4−d. The coefficient encodes short-distance dynamics and can be a matrix in flavour space.

Effective field theory OurBigBook.com
An ultraviolet completion specifies a theory valid at higher energies whose low-energy limit gives an effective field theory. For large-field cosmic inflation, it may also need to control the potential over a large field range, which is distinct from the energy scale of a process.

A large field value alone does not establish Planckian energy density or invalidate every possible completion.

A local field operator is built from fields and finitely many of their derivatives at one spacetime point. Its integral can deform an action, with the operator's scaling dimension determining the engineering dimension of the associated coupling.

An observable unchanged by adding a particle with vanishing energy or replacing one massless particle by exactly collinear particles with the same total momentum. Fully inclusive electron-positron hadronic rates and suitably defined jet observables are examples.

A singularity of a massless scattering or radiation integral when momenta of two particles become parallel. In Quantum chromodynamics, unresolved quark-gluon splittings cause such divergences. Spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when the action and equations have a symmetry but a chosen ground state is invariant only under a proper subgroup. Acting with the broken symmetry generates a degenerate vacuum manifold.

Vacuum manifold OurBigBook.com
A spatially homogeneous field value minimizing the potential energy. For a finite-energy field configuration on an infinite domain, the potential is normally shifted so the relevant vacuum energy density is zero. Disconnected components of the vacuum manifold allow a scalar-field kink to connect distinct vacuum values.

Vacuum manifold OurBigBook.com
A scalar-field vacuum is a constant field at a minimum of its potential energy, with the minimum shifted to zero when discussing finite-energy classical field-theory solitons. Distinct isolated vacua allow a scalar-field kink to approach different values at the two ends of space.

V=ϕ2[24λ​(ϕ−λ2μ​)2+2m2​−6λμ2​].
(5)
Thus zero is a global minimum precisely when μ2≤3λm2. At a nontrivial equality there are degenerate minima at zero and 2μ/λ. If m2>0 and the inequality fails, zero is a false vacuum: its Hessian is positive but another minimum has lower energy. A local minimum of the scalar potential that has higher energy than a global minimum. A classical field theory is a gauge theory when its description has a local redundancy represented by gauge transformations. Physically equivalent gauge descriptions must give the same observables, even though the gauge potential changes.

Its Feynman rules assign 1/m2 to each propagator, −λ to each quartic vertex, and the reciprocal Feynman-diagram symmetry factor to each vacuum diagram. The integral itself includes disconnected vacuum diagrams; its logarithm selects connected ones. At second order the three possible numbers of edges joining the two vertices are zero, two and four, with Feynman-diagram symmetry factors 128,16,48 respectively. Their weights add to 35λ2/(384m8).
The Wick contractions give the general coefficient I(0)(−1)v(4v−1)!!/[v!(4!)vm4v]. Successive absolute coefficients have ratio (4v+3)(4v+1)/[24(v+1)m4], which tends to infinity. An imaginary-time-ordered correlation function orders operators along the Euclidean thermal circle. Bosonic correlators are periodic with period β.

The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger condition uses cyclicity of the thermal trace to relate correlation functions separated by imaginary time β.

Bosonic Matsubara frequencies are ωn​=2πnT. They are the Fourier modes on the periodic imaginary-time circle.

For E>0, contour summation over bosonic Matsubara frequencies gives
T∑n∈Z​ωn2​+E21​=2E1​coth2TE​.
(20)
It separates into the zero-point term 1/(2E) and a thermal Bose--Einstein occupation term.

Large-N expansion (large-N expansion)

Words: 95 Articles: 3
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The large-N expansion organizes an O(N)-symmetric theory in powers of 1/N. At leading order, an auxiliary constraint field is determined by a self-consistent saddle-point or gap equation.

Gap equation

Words: 66 Articles: 2
Large-N expansion OurBigBook.com
A gap equation determines a physical mass or excitation gap self-consistently from an interaction and a regulated fluctuation integral.

Critical coupling (gc​)

Words: 27
Gap equation OurBigBook.com
A critical coupling is a coupling value at which a gap equation first admits a massless solution. Tuning through it can separate symmetric gapped and symmetry-broken phases.

Words: 20
Gap equation OurBigBook.com
At an upper critical dimension, a nominal power-law critical scaling acquires a multiplicative logarithmic correction because the coupling is marginal.

Path integral

Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A path integral represents a quantum amplitude or correlation function as an integral over field histories weighted by the exponential of the action.

Time-sliced configuration-space path integral

Words: 45
Path integral OurBigBook.com
For a Hamiltonian operator with kinetic term p^​2/2, insert position-basis resolutions between Trotter product formula factors. The measure is the limit of (2πiΔ)−M/2∏j=1M−1​dqj​, and the exponent contains ∑j​[(qj​−qj−1​)2/(2Δ)−ΔV(qj−1​)]. Its continuum notation is ∫DqeiS[q], with fixed endpoint values. A damping prescription defines the oscillatory limit.

Gaussian path integral (∫Dηei⟨η,Aη⟩∝(detA)−1)

Words: 146 Articles: 2
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A quadratic path integral becomes a product of Gaussian integrals after diagonalizing its fluctuation operator. One real coordinate per mode gives an inverse square root of the functional determinant; one complex coordinate, or two real coordinates, gives its inverse. A regulator and normalization are essential: determinant ratios are often meaningful before an absolute determinant is defined.

Classical-path factorization of a quadratic path integral (K(qf​,qi​;T)=N(T)eiS[qc​])

Words: 56
Gaussian path integral OurBigBook.com
For a quadratic potential energy, shifting a path to its classical solution leaves an exactly quadratic fluctuation action with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The first variation vanishes by the Euler-Lagrange equation. The Gaussian path integral prefactor is an inverse square root of a regulated functional determinant and does not depend on the endpoints. At conjugate times the ordinary formula must instead be read by distributional continuation.

Dirichlet oscillator determinant ratio (det(−∂t2​−ω2)/det(−∂t2​)=sin(ωT)/(ωT))

Words: 41
Gaussian path integral OurBigBook.com
On [0,T] with vanishing endpoint fluctuations, the sine-mode eigenvalues are (πn/T)2−ω2. Divide by the free eigenvalues and use the sine infinite product. The ratio determines the harmonic oscillator transition kernel once the free configuration-space path integral is normalized. Zeros correspond to caustics where the fluctuation operator has a zero mode.

Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation (∫dMe−M2/(2U)+Mj∝eUj2/2)

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A Gaussian auxiliary-field identity replacing a quadratic expression in a composite field by a linear coupling to a new field. Completing the square in M2/(2U)−Mj yields an exponential eUj2/2 after integrating M, with normalized Gaussian prefactors. It converts suitable quartic field interactions into bilinear couplings and permits fermionic fields to be integrated out.

Spin-vector Hubbard–Stratonovich decoupling (j2=−6ψˉ​↑​ψˉ​↓​ψ↓​ψ↑​)

Words: 41
Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation OurBigBook.com
For two Grassmann spin components, j=ψˉ​σψ satisfies j2=−6ψˉ​↑​ψˉ​↓​ψ↓​ψ↑​. A real vector auxiliary field with cost M2/(2U) and coupling −M⋅j therefore reproduces the repulsive 3U contact action. All three spin components are essential to that normalization.

Coherent-state time slicing

Words: 145 Articles: 2
Path integral OurBigBook.com
Insert the coherent-state resolution of identity between short-time evolution operators. For a normally ordered Hamiltonian, the kernel uses the next bra label and current ket label: ⟨ψj+1​∣e−ϵH∣ψj​⟩=exp(ψˉ​j+1​ψj​−ϵH(ψˉ​j+1​,ψj​)+O(ϵ2)). Together with the Gaussian measure this yields the first-order derivative term ψˉ​∂τ​ψ. The adjacent-label prescription retains operator ordering information that a formal continuum expression alone can hide.

Coherent-state thermal boundary conditions (ψ(β)=ζψ(0))

Words: 91 Articles: 1
Coherent-state time slicing OurBigBook.com
The thermal trace closes bosonic coherent-state paths periodically and fermionic coherent-state paths antiperiodically: ψ(β)=ζψ(0) and ψˉ​(β)=ζψˉ​(0), with ζ=1 for bosons and −1 for fermions. The minus sign follows from the fermionic coherent-state trace, not from choosing a different Hamiltonian. These boundary conditions determine the allowed Matsubara frequencies.
Fermionic one-level thermal determinant (detAP​(∂τ​+ξ)=1+e−βξ)
Words: 46
Coherent-state thermal boundary conditions OurBigBook.com
An antiperiodic free fermion field with inverse propagator ∂τ​+ξ has a thermally normalized determinant 1+e−βξ. The factor counts empty and occupied states of one level. Its logarithmic Matsubara sum is meaningful only with a regularization fixing the determinant normalization; an unqualified infinite product is not convergent.

Scalar field path integral (Z[J]=∫Dϕei(S[ϕ]+∫Jϕ))

Words: 123 Articles: 2
Path integral OurBigBook.com
The scalar field path integral generalizes the configuration-space path integral by replacing finitely many coordinates with field values. Its regulated measure integrates one field variable at every spacetime lattice point. Fixed boundary fields give transition kernels; vacuum boundary conditions and sources give the normalized vacuum generating functional.

Path-integral perturbation by source derivatives (Z[J]∝eiSint​[(1/i)δ/δJ]Z0​[J])

Words: 42
Scalar field path integral OurBigBook.com
An interaction depending on the field can be represented by substituting (1/i)δ/δJ into its action and acting on the free generating functional. Expanding that exponential produces Feynman diagrams, contractions and vertex weights. Normalize by the resulting value at J=0 to cancel vacuum diagrams.

Vacuum projection by imaginary time (e−TH∣n⟩=e−TEn​∣n⟩)

Words: 44
Scalar field path integral OurBigBook.com
Long imaginary-time evolution multiplies an energy eigenstate by e−TEn​. After normalization it projects onto the lowest energy component with nonzero initial overlap, or onto the lowest-energy subspace if the vacuum is degenerate. This provides vacuum boundary conditions for a path integral and is related to the Feynman i-epsilon prescription.

Configuration-space path integral (K(qf​,qi​)=∫qi​qf​​DqeiS[q])

Words: 149 Articles: 2
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A configuration-space path integral integrates histories of the coordinates with weight eiS. Fixed endpoint conditions specify a transition amplitude. For a quadratic kinetic energy it follows by Gaussian momentum integration from the phase-space path integral. Time-slicing fixes the normalization, and a regulator gives meaning to the otherwise formal functional measure.

Classical path (qc​(t))

Words: 61
Configuration-space path integral OurBigBook.com
A classical path joining prescribed endpoints is a stationary point of the action, satisfying the Euler-Lagrange equation and the endpoint boundary conditions. Expanding the path integral about each such path separates its classical phase from its quadratic fluctuation determinant. There may be multiple classical paths or none within a chosen real saddle class; the semiclassical propagator must respect that saddle structure rather than assuming a unique trajectory for every potential.

Euclidean configuration-space transition kernel (⟨qf​∣e−Hτ/ℏ∣qi​⟩)

Words: 43
Configuration-space path integral OurBigBook.com
For H=p2/(2m)+V(q), time slicing gives a Euclidean path integral over paths with the specified endpoints and action SE​=∫[mq˙​2/2+V(q)]dt. Each step contributes normalization (m/(2πℏδ))1/2. This normalization fixes the units and endpoint factors of the kernel, which differ from amplitudes between normalized localized wavepackets.

Phase-space path integral (K=∫DqDpei∫(pq˙​−H)dt)

Words: 183 Articles: 3
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A phase-space path integral represents a quantum transition kernel by integrating both coordinates and conjugate momenta with action ∫(pq˙​−H)dt. It follows from inserting position and momentum completeness relations between short-time evolution operators. For a quadratic momentum dependence the momentum variables can be integrated by a Gaussian integral.

Words: 100 Articles: 1
Phase-space path integral OurBigBook.com
Integrating each momentum in a quadratic Hamiltonian yields the configuration-space kinetic action and its time-slice normalization. A raw dp measure gives 2πm/Δt​; the normalized Fourier measure dp/(2π) gives m/(2πΔt)​. Dropping the time dependence changes the quantum-mechanical propagator.
Time-sliced equivalence of phase-space and configuration-space path integrals
Words: 60
Gaussian momentum integration in a phase-space path integral OurBigBook.com
For H=p2/(2m)+V(q), time slices of length δ use N momentum measures dpj​/(2πℏ) and N−1 intermediate coordinate measures. Each momentum Gaussian integral gives [m/(2πiℏδ)]1/2exp[im(qj​−qj−1​)2/(2ℏδ)]. The resulting configuration integral has normalization [m/(2πiℏδ)]N/2. A common endpoint convention for V and the Trotter product formula identify both limits with the same operator transition kernel; a damping or imaginary-time prescription defines the oscillatory integrals.

The first-order term means ∑i​pi​(qi+1​−qi​) in a finite-dimensional integral. Specify the endpoints and an ordering prescription, then take the maximum time step to zero. Typical Euclidean paths are not classically differentiable, so the discrete prescription is essential.

Euclidean path integral (Z=∫Dϕe−SE​[ϕ])

Path integral OurBigBook.com
A path integral with weight e−SE​ uses the Euclidean action obtained by Wick rotation. Bosonic convergence requires appropriate positivity and boundary conditions.

Instanton

Words: 449 Articles: 7
Euclidean path integral OurBigBook.com
An instanton is a localized finite-action classical solution in Euclidean spacetime, used in a semiclassical description of quantum tunnelling and other nonperturbative effects. In one-dimensional quantum mechanics it can connect distinct degenerate potential minima over infinite Euclidean time. A quartic double-well instanton is an elementary example; a Yang-Mills instanton is a gauge-field example with different geometric structure.
Euclidean bounce
Words: 81
Instanton OurBigBook.com
A Euclidean bounce is a finite-action Euclidean saddle associated with decay of a false vacuum. It returns to the same metastable vacuum at the two ends of Euclidean time, instead of joining two degenerate stable vacua. Its characteristic negative fluctuation direction produces the imaginary part associated with a decay rate; the leading semiclassical suppression is e−SB​/ℏ. Translation zero modes are treated as collective coordinates. It should not be confused with the stable double-well tunnelling instanton whose repeated crossings give a real level splitting.
Anti-instanton
Words: 41
Instanton OurBigBook.com
The orientation-reversed Euclidean trajectory of an instanton. In a symmetric double well it goes from the right vacuum to the left vacuum and has the same positive action as the forward crossing. Its topological orientation changes sign, not its Euclidean action.
Dilute instanton gas (κ=Ke−SI​/ℏ≪ω)
Words: 62
Instanton OurBigBook.com
When individual instantons are much narrower than their typical separation, multi-crossing paths factor at leading semiclassical order. Integrating n ordered centers over time τ contributes τn/n!. In a double well, crossings alternate direction and even/odd counts yield hyperbolic cosine/sine amplitudes. This approximation requires large action relative to ℏ, matched local well structure and control of corrections from interactions and local anharmonicity.
Instanton fluctuation prefactor (K=SI​/(2πℏ)​[detL0​/det′LI​]1/2)
Words: 129 Articles: 1
Instanton OurBigBook.com
For a one-dimensional quantum tunnelling instanton, the prefactor combines nonzero Gaussian fluctuation eigenvalues with the translation zero-mode Jacobian. Here LI​=−∂t2​+V′′(qI​)/m, L0​=−∂t2​+ω2, and the prime excludes the zero mode. Common endpoint regularization and reference normalization define the determinant ratio. The resulting K has frequency units, while Ke−SI​/ℏ is the dilute crossing rate. This determinant/collective-coordinate structure is also discussed in Dunne, Sulejmanpasic and Ünsal's treatment; unequal neighbouring well frequencies require care and need not share the symmetric-double-well result.
Instanton translation zero mode (LI​q˙​I​=0)
Words: 54
Instanton fluctuation prefactor OurBigBook.com
Differentiating the Euclidean classical equation for an instanton gives a zero eigenfunction proportional to its time derivative. Its norm satisfies μ∫q˙​I2​dτ=SI​, so replacing the Gaussian zero-mode integral by the center coordinate gives SI​/(2πℏ)​dτ0​. The nonzero modes belong in the primed functional determinant. This removes the false divergence without deleting the center's integration volume.

Instanton OurBigBook.com
For V(q)=mω2(q2−a2)2/(8a2), the zero Euclidean-energy condition is mq˙​2/2=V(q). Integrating gives the displayed instanton from −a to a. Its action is ∫−aa​2mV(q)​dq=2mωa2/3. The arbitrary center t0​ supplies a translation zero mode, treated as a collective coordinate in the instanton fluctuation prefactor.

Quartic double-well instanton OurBigBook.com
The quartic double-well instanton has LI​=−∂τ2​+ω2[1−3sech2(ωτ/2)/2]. For a positive regulator ε and r=21+ε/ω2​, the common infinite-line determinant ratio is (r−1)(r−2)/[(r+1)(r+2)]. Its zero-mode factor is ε/(12ω2) to leading order, giving the displayed primed ratio. Therefore the instanton fluctuation prefactor is K=ω6SI​/(πℏ)​ and the double-well tunneling splitting is 2ℏKe−SI​/ℏ.

Operator-path-integral equivalence

Words: 62
Path integral OurBigBook.com
With a time-slice regulator, inserting field-coordinate resolutions of identity in evolution kernels produces a bosonic phase-space path integral; integrating the canonical momentum gives the configuration-space action. For fermions, resolutions in fermionic coherent states instead produce a Berezin integral and the first-order kinetic term. Vacuum endpoint projection supplies the Feynman i-epsilon prescription. Both constructions reproduce the same free oscillator correlators and their Wick theorem expansions, and thus agree order by order in a regulated perturbation series.

Euclidean worldline path integral

Words: 136 Articles: 1
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A thermal path integral represents the canonical partition function by paths periodic in Euclidean time of circumference β. For H=p2/2+V(x), its formal action is SE​[x]=∫0β​(x˙2/2+V(x))dτ. The periodic boundary condition results from taking the trace of the evolution kernel. The continuum measure requires a regularization and normalization; finite-dimensional measures make both choices explicit.

Fourier-cutoff oscillator functional determinant (ZN​=AN​ω−1∏r=1N​(ω2+νr2​)−1)

Words: 88
Euclidean worldline path integral OurBigBook.com
Use an orthonormal real Fourier series basis on a circle of length β, with νr​=2πr/β. Retain the constant coefficient and the sine/cosine pair for each 1≤r≤N. The oscillator action becomes 21​ω2q02​+21​∑r​(ω2+νr2​)(qr2​+sr2​). A product of real Gaussian integrals gives the displayed functional determinant, with AN​ independent of ω. Ratios for two frequencies converge regardless of AN​. The absolute limit requires its normalization: AN​=β−1∏r​νr2​ gives the thermal partition function of a quantum harmonic oscillator in the limit. Multiplying this choice by an oscillating positive sequence preserves all frequency ratios but destroys the absolute limit.

The functional measure is the formal integration measure over field configurations in a path integral. Its transformation under a symmetry can preserve the corresponding Ward identity or produce a quantum anomaly.
